arguments.data: rdi; pointer to the input bytes. Read on every path, never written
arguments.length: rsi; the input length in bytes. Both entries gate on length >= 241. Inside the body the length selects the full-block count (length >> 10), the remainder stripe count ((length >> 6) & 0xf), the final-stripe gate (length & 63) and the merge start value (length * PRIME64_1)
arguments.third_register: rdx; never read anywhere in the window. The with-seed parent enters with it still holding the tested seed (0 on that path); the sibling entry enters with its own third argument in place. One payload under four rdx values gives one result in the differential

census.direct_calls_note: no e8 call site targets the window; it is entered only by the two tail jumps below
census.tail_jumps_note: 0x61c2cf3 sits in the with-seed hash-long body (FDE 0x61c2cb0..0x61c3221), its seed==0 exit: the seed is tested at 0x61c2cd0, the stack canary is verified at 0x61c2cd5..0x61c2ce6 and the frame restored before the jump, with (data, length) already in the argument registers. 0x61c3b50 sits in the sibling length-dispatching hash entry (FDE 0x61c38a0..0x61c3bb9); control reaches it when the compare at 0x61c3a88 finds the length above 0xf0 (ja 0x61c3b50). Both sites confirmed as real jmp instructions by linear disassembly of their containing FDEs (objdump). Per-site rows are in callers.tsv

entry_paths.gate: the parent with-seed body is itself entered for lengths >= 241 (its own entry, from the hash callee at 0x61c3530); on entry it tests the seed at 0x61c2cd0 and, when the seed is zero, verifies its stack canary, restores its frame and jumps here at 0x61c2cf3 with (data, length) untouched
entry_paths.kind: tail jump (seed==0 exit of the with-seed hash-long body)

entry_paths.gate: inside the sibling length-dispatching entry, the arm at 0x61c3a88 compares the length against 0xf0 and jumps here (via 0x61c3b50) when the length is above 240; the argument registers carry the sibling's own (data, length)
entry_paths.kind: tail jump (sibling hash entry, lengths above 240)

final_mix: the merge routine at 0x61c27f0, called once at 0x61c2c8e with rdi = the stack accumulator array, rsi = 0x97df0b (the secret table + 11), rdx = length * PRIME64_1; its return value is this body's result. The merge body is pinned by its own packet (RE-001-hash-merge-accs-61c27f0-115, PR #3533): per pair i it folds fold(acc[2i] ^ rd64(secret, 11 + 16*i), acc[2i+1] ^ rd64(secret, 11 + 16*i + 8)) with fold(x, y) = lo(x*y) ^ hi(x*y), sums the four folds with the start value, and avalanches (y = x ^ (x >> 37); y *= 0x165667b19e3779f9; y ^ (y >> 32))

length_arms.1024 and up: length >> 10 full blocks (16 stripes plus a scramble each), then the remainder stripes and the final stripe as below
length_arms.241..1023: no full block: (length >> 6) remainder stripes (3..15), the secret window sliding +8 per stripe from offset 0, then the final stripe when length & 63 != 0
length_arms.length % 64 == 0: no final stripe runs: the last 64 bytes are covered by a block or remainder stripe at a sliding secret offset, never by the offset-121 window

mix_primitive: per qword lane of a stripe: x = data ^ SECRET[window + lane]; acc[lane] += data + lo32(x) * hi32(x) (the two 32-bit halves of the xored value, multiplied into one 64-bit product). The window slides +8 per stripe within a stripe sequence

primes.init: [PRIME32_3, PRIME64_1, PRIME64_2, PRIME64_3, PRIME64_4, PRIME32_2, PRIME64_5, PRIME32_1] = [0xc2b2ae3d, 0x9e3779b185ebca87, 0xc2b2ae3d27d4eb4f, 0x165667b19e3779f9, 0x85ebca77c2b2ae63, 0x85ebca77, 0x27d4eb2f165667c5, 0x9e3779b1]
primes.p1: 0x9e3779b185ebca87 (the merge start multiplier: start = length * PRIME64_1)
primes.prime32_1: 0x9e3779b1 (the scramble multiplier, applied as a full 64x32 product per accumulator)
primes.prime_mix: 0x165667b19e3779f9 (the merge avalanche multiplier, inside the merge routine)

return_value: rax: the 64-bit hash of the input under the default secret, for lengths 241 and up

secret_table.note: the 192-byte table at VA 0x97df00 in .rodata, the same table the rest of the hash family cites. The stripe sequences read it from memory through a sliding pointer; the scramble keys and the final stripe's window are its entries baked in as .rodata constant vectors (verified entry by entry against the table): scramble keys are the qwords at offsets 128..192, the final stripe's pairs are the qwords at offsets 121 + 16*j and 121 + 16*j + 8

offsets_used.merge_window: +11 (the merge routine reads its 64-byte window at 0x97df0b)
offsets_used.stripes: 8*k + 16*j per stripe k, pair j (qwords at 8*k + 16*j and 8*k + 16*j + 8)

semantics.block_loop: length >> 10 iterations (outer loop head 0x61c2930); each block runs 16 stripes over data + block*1024 + 64*k with the secret pointer walking 0x97df00..0x97df80 (+8 per stripe, inner loop 0x61c2940..0x61c29fb) and then scrambles
semantics.final_stripe: only when length & 63 != 0 (test at 0x61c2bc2): one accumulate step over data + length - 64 with the secret window at offset 121, accumulating straight into the stack array (0x61c2bcc..0x61c2c71)
semantics.init: the eight accumulators start at the prime ladder (constant vectors stored to the stack array at 0x61c28d2..0x61c28e1) and are held in xmm register pairs across the stripe loops
semantics.merge_call: at 0x61c2c76..0x61c2c8e: rdx = length * 0x9e3779b185ebca87, rsi = 0x97df0b, rdi = rsp (the accumulator array); call 0x61c27f0; the canary is then verified (0x61c2c93..0x61c2ca1) and the body returns the merge result
semantics.remainder_stripes: count = (length >> 6) & 0xf (0x61c2ac8..0x61c2adf), skipped when zero; stripes over data + (length & ~0x3ff) + 64*k (loop 0x61c2b00..0x61c2ba8) with the secret pointer reset to 0x97df00 and again sliding +8 per stripe, ending at secret + 8*count; the accumulator pairs are stored back to the stack array afterwards
semantics.scramble: after each block (0x61c2a01..0x61c2aab), per accumulator i: acc[i] = (acc[i] ^ (acc[i] >> 47) ^ SECRET[128 + 8*i]) * PRIME32_1, the multiply done as the pmuludq pair (lo32 * PRIME32_1) + ((hi32 * PRIME32_1) << 32)

side_effects: writes only its own 0x58-byte stack frame: the 64-byte accumulator array the merge call receives, and the stack-canary slot at frame + 0x48 (stored at 0x61c28ab, verified against %fs:0x28 before ret; a mismatch calls __stack_chk_fail@plt). The only other call is to the merge routine at 0x61c27f0. The input is read, never written; callee-saved registers are preserved (the body touches none of rbx, rbp, r12-r15)
unknowns: the exact source spelling of the function; the RE-002 vendor census registers this window as XXPH3_hashLong_64b_defaultSecret (librocksdb-sys 0.11.0+8.1.1) — that identity is the census's claim and is consistent with everything pinned here (the default-secret table, the prime-ladder init, the sliding stripe windows, the offset-121 final stripe, the merge at secret + 11), but this packet pins the target body's own semantics and neither needs nor re-claims the identity
the sibling entry body's own semantics (FDE 0x61c38a0..0x61c3bb9): only its delegation site and the 0xf0 length gate are claimed here, not the sibling's arms

why the remainder stripe count takes the (length >> 6) & 0xf form rather than a (length - 1) form; the count is pinned as written, and the behaviour it produces at length % 64 == 0 (no final stripe) is covered by the differential
